All required lands are presently held in fee ownership by Crescent Land and Timber Corporation, a wholly owned subsidiary of Duke Power Company. General land configuration and locations of proposed project facilities are depicted by Figure 1-3. Quarries, borrow, and spoil areas are depicted by Figure 1-4.
Of the 820 acres required, almost all are presently occupied by second growth forest. About 1.3 acres of Bad and West Bad Creeks would be inundated. The only man-made structure affected within the 820-acre area involved would be approximately 0.4 mile of South Carolina State Highway No. 171 located on the western border of the proposed project and which would be relocated.
The upper reservoir, including the damsites, would occupy 370 acres. An access road about 4 miles long and a switchyard would require 95 acres. Three-hundred-fifteen acres would be required for the new 200-foot-wide transmission line corridor and alteration of the existing corridor. (Three of these acres would be required for transmission line towers.) During construction, an additional 40 acres would be cleared for use as a construction yard site and spoil area. The remaining acreage would be occupied by two dams, a saddle dike, powerhouse, tunnel, and appurtenant project works.
No new lands would be required for a lower reservoir since the proposed pumped storage project would utilize existing Lake Jocassee as its lower pool.
A 31-mile hiking trail and related features would be constructed by the Applicant as an adjunct to the proposed project, but outside the project boundary. Portions of the trail would be located near the Toxaway River arm of Lake Jocassee (FPC Project No. 2503). The trail would consist of a cleared passage 4 feet wide and 8 feet high through the forest understory, with a 2-foot-wide footpath.
All lands required for the Bad Creek Project would be located within the Horsepasture Game Management Area, administered for wildlife management by the South Carolina Wildlife and Marine Resources Department and within the proclamation boundary of Sumter National Forest. Of the 820 acres required for the project, approximately 505 acres would be permanently occupied by the upper reservoir and other project facilities.
